item.title: [No Priors: AI, Machine Learning, Tech, & Startups] Redefining Chip Architecture with Arm CEO Rene Haas
item.dc:creator: No Priors: AI, Machine Learning, Tech, & Startups
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、CPU 的"隐身悖论"：为什么被遗忘反而是护城河

Renee 提到一个极具反讽意味的现象——当 ChatGPT 引爆 AI 浪潮时，"无论问题是什么，答案都是加速器"。CPU 被集体遗忘。但这恰恰是 ARM 最深的护城河所在。

一个出人意料的观察：CPU 的战略价值不来自它做什么，而来自它是"token 的搬运工"而非"token 的制造者"。GPU 是生产线，但没有搬运工，产品堆在工厂里毫无价值。这与物流业的历史惊人相似——19 世纪末所有人关注钢铁厂（生产端），但真正累积复利财富的是范德比尔特这样的铁路运输大王（编排端）。编排层永远比生产层活得久，因为它是系统的语法，而生产层只是词汇。

这也解释了为什么 ARM 敢在 98.5% 毛利的"完美生意"上冒险转型做实体芯片——他们意识到编排者的位置一旦被系统重构撼动，纯 IP 授权模式就会像 90 年代的 Sun Microsystems 一样被架空。

二、"不可训练性"作为新型知识产权：AI 时代最反直觉的资产

Renee 无意中说出了本轮对话最深的洞见——"如果没有文档，它就无法使用；无法使用就无法测试；无法测试就无法训练；无法训练就在 AI 时代无用。"

这是一个哲学层面的断裂：在前 AI 时代，"专有 = 有价值"；在 AI 时代，"可训练 = 有价值"。ARM 的真正护城河不是 IP 本身，而是几十年积累的测试台、文档、失败记录——这些以前被视为工程负担的东西，现在成了训练语料的黄金矿脉。

跨领域连接：这与生物医药领域正在发生的转变完全对应。过去药企的核心资产是分子专利；现在真正稀缺的是高质量的临床失败数据——因为 AI 药物发现模型需要"负样本"才能学会什么不该合成。ARM 的文档就是芯片界的"临床失败记录"。

这意味着一条隐藏的产业法则：未来 5 年，企业的可训练资产盘点将比资产负债表更能预测其市值。

三、"数据中心恐惧症"的真正结构：不是关于 AI，而是关于阶级

Renee 谈到公众对数据中心的反弹时，触及了一个更深的社会学模式——但他自己可能没意识到全貌。

一个打破常规的解读：数据中心之所以成为众矢之的，恰恰是因为它"看起来无害"——一个大盒子、两辆车、无人值守。这种"视觉上的无劳动性"激活了一种深层的社会创伤：当劳动的可见性消失时，普通人失去了参与经济叙事的入口。相比之下，电工工会公开支持数据中心建设——因为他们看得见管线、看得见工时。

这与19 世纪反机器主义（勒德运动）的心理结构一模一样，但形态倒转了：勒德分子砸的是看得见的机器；今天的反数据中心运动攻击的是看不见的智能。Renee 说"这是恐惧"，但更精确的说法是——这是对"经济叙事排除"的恐惧，而不是对失业本身的恐惧。

一个意外的推论：这意味着 AI 行业要化解这场舆论战，靠的不是数据（"我们创造了 X 个工作"），而是让 AI 的劳动重新变得可见——比如展示数据中心里巡检的电工、液冷工程师、变电站建设工人。这与政治学中"具象化让位于抽象化"必然引发民粹反弹的规律完全一致。

四、隐藏的时间悖论：AI 加速设计，但供应链延长瓶颈

Renee 预测 5-10 年内芯片设计周期可能从 24-36 个月压缩到 6-12 个月。但同时他又说供应链紧张会持续 3-5 年以上。

这里藏着一个反直觉的产业动力学：设计速度越快，供应链瓶颈就越严重——因为传统的"设计慢"其实是供应链的天然缓冲。当 AI 把设计时间砍掉 70%，芯片行业将进入一个类似服装快时尚 vs. 纺织产能的失衡状态——ZARA 可以两周出新款，但棉花种植周期没变。

这预示着未来 5 年会出现一个全新的商业物种："芯片供应链套利者"——他们不设计芯片，而是提前锁定 3nm 产能、封装线、HBM 内存配额，然后以类似"航空公司超售机票"的模式打包卖给设计公司。这不是 Renee 明说的，但这正是他反复强调"资本 + 生态关系"是新守门人时的潜台词。

从 IP 授权到自研 CPU：为什么现在？

Why'd you make the move now? So for, you know, ARM, I believe, existed for a few decades now. The focus was always on IP, which is effectively like designing the way that different chip components are put together. Then you licensed that out to other people to actually manufacture and incorporate into their designs. Why did you decide to start making some of your own CPUs?

Yeah, it was an evolution from the early days of where we just supplied simply the IP components, the pieces, the CPU IP, the GPU IP, the system IP, etc., etc.

Few years ago, what we were starting to see was that product cycle times aren't slowing down. Chip manufacturing times are extending. The ability to get solutions out faster was becoming more and more important. So we moved from these individual components into what we called compute subsystems.

I used, when we went did the road show a few years ago, I used the Lego analogy where essentially we're providing the blueprint on here's how you stitch it all together. Demand for that was insane. And what we were finding was — we initially people thought well people aren't going to want these subsystems because that's what a chip designer does. Why are you providing that piece? But it saved time to market and it saved a whole lot of things in terms of cost, speed, etc., etc.

The physical product was sort of the next leap, if you will. And there are certain sets of customers that will license IP to and they've got all the capability in the world to build chips based on ARM. There's a lot of companies who want to have product based on ARM. Not all of our customers build products that serve those markets.

So Meta was that first example. They wanted a general purpose agentic CPU. There wasn't anybody out who could give it to them. They came to us and said, "Hey why don't we do this together," and that's how we got into it.

生态系统的反应

How has that landed with the rest of your customer base?

So one of the things that we were very careful about was getting making sure the ecosystem was on board with this because we do CPU IP which is really only as good as the ecosystem. The ecosystem of chip people and the ecosystem of software folks and people who build around that.

So we talked to just about everybody who were customers and said, "You know how do you feel about this as direction we're going?" And surprisingly we got a lot less pushback than I thought and the reason for that was the more software that's available in the wild — whether it's proprietary and/or open-source — benefits the broader ecosystem and the customers themselves.

So whether it was Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, Google, all people who build ARM-based server chips, they were all on board. And I think the ultimate proof point was when we announced the product last March, we had Jensen, we had Ronnie Boker, we had Amen, we had James Hamilton — you know, all the folks from those customers I mentioned all saying congratulations. Yeah. So we obviously to deliver a product — and we're a fabless semi company, right? Yeah. Kind of beautiful.

After that, go to the library that we have down the hall that's got all the books that you can go up and look all this information up.

出口管制与"无限游戏"

You know, as far as the export controls go and, "We're going to limit the chips because we don't want China to win the race," you know, end quote. My personal view is that it's an infinite game. But ultimately, and I'm a big believer of this, number one, for both national security reasons and economic, you want to be at the forefront of technology because it drives innovation, but it also drives ecosystems.

If you think about the US auto industry in the 1950s post-World War II where Detroit was the center of the universe — you had spots across Wisconsin, Ohio, Illinois, whether it was Firestone or Bridgestone (Bridgestone Japanese), but other companies in that ecosystem that fed into it.

Data centers are kind of the same way. People look at data centers and say, "Oh, it's a big Costco box and there's two cars in the parking lot and all of that is being driven automatically, so there's no jobs." I call BS on that because if you think about whether it's around energy, liquid cooling, all of the things that make the data center better — those are all jobs that can be created and done here.

So I think as a national policy, it's incredibly important for us to be investing in the United States and making sure that we stay in the lead.

数据中心反弹背后的社会心理

On the data center side in particular, it seems like a lot of the actions that are being taken to try and prevent future data centers feel more coordinated than not. I know it's phrases "grassroots efforts" but it seems like there's some coordinated function there. Do you have a hypothesis in terms of why there's been this sudden unexpected outcry on data centers from certain corners?

I think there is — we were maybe chatting about this a bit earlier — that there's a fear that AI means job loss and job loss means for all these things kind of implications. So I think unfortunately —

You think that fear is well grounded or — because somewhere it seems like it's only creating jobs.

No, I think — I don't think it's well grounded at all.

I think the electricians labor union specifically said, "Please don't ban the data centers. We need these jobs" very recently.

Oh completely. Yeah, I mean these are jobs that — people, that's a great example, right? Because here's one where there may have been a stigma to being an electrician, right? Electrician is either not maybe viewed as a highly educated job or you don't need a PhD. It's a highly skilled job that requires a lot of training and certification and you need tons of them, you know, to do this kind of work. And that's very, very critical to the data centers.

So I think to your question, I think part of the backlash is just from fear. Just there's a fear that my jobs are going to go away. The AI boom for good or for bad has benefited a lot of people and there's a lot of people who have no benefit from it, right?

And there's a lot of America, just again on the American political scene, who it's tough to make the mortgage, you know, their paychecks haven't gone up, and now they've got this AI thing that just looks going to even harder. So I think the data centers become a bullseye unfortunately for all the things that could be bad about AI, which I think is just people are holding up like fake tainted water and claiming that, you know, it's ruining the water supply. So I feel like there's other kind of things that are just being made up about data centers as a way to try and create fear.

For sure. Yeah. For sure. And unfortunately it's become the boogeyman for a lot of things.

做行业领导者的意义

I think it's also pretty clear that there's like, you know, organized media influence around these issues as well. But I think you can have all three separate points here including yours, Renee, which is there are benefits from the construction of essentially like a rapidly growing new industry that can create new technology and new jobs and create, you know, external wealth for the communities around them. But it's on the industry to go communicate that.

Yeah. I mean, on first principles, whether it was smartphones, the internet, personal computers — fill in your favorite technology — there is no downside from being the leader.

There's just not.

This is maybe the most important point.

There's just not downside from being the leader. There are second and third order effects that you may not like, but to be the laggard — you are having the entire script dictated to you and everything that kind of comes with it.

I mean look at other parts of the world that are just not the leaders in this space economically and socially — they're left behind and governments carry the large tax burden of it. So if you're on the wave of some technology innovation, and I would argue to some extent AI is a little bit of the final frontier of what can be done with essentially intelligence — of course you want to be in the lead. Of course you want to be driving that because the benefits for society are going to be enormous.

ARM 未来的兴奋点

What are you most excited about in the coming year or two for ARM?

Being in the center of all that. Yeah. Honestly, I think we are — I feel fortunate every day that we are in the heart of all of this and the fact that we can be a participant in that ecosystem. We can help drive the innovation. We can be involved with leadership companies, develop leadership products.

We're right in the middle of it all because all the AI needs some level of compute. That's what ARM does. And that compute needs to be power efficient. That's what we're really, really good at. So those roads all lead through us.

So, you know, been in this industry my entire career had a lot of times thinking about, "Gosh, what's the next product we're going to need? Do people really need another tablet and does it need to be 8.9 inches or 9.2 inches?" And now it's — I there's no — the abundance of opportunity innovation is so great with AI. So yeah, I'm super excited and feel blessed to be leading a company that's in the center of it all.

CPU 在 AI 时代的核心角色

The need for chips is driven by like massive change in workload, right? And we have continual massive change in workload. So no better place, time to, you know, go work on chip designs and sell to all the people working on that innovation.

My understanding of the CPU opportunity in this era is like two core pieces and then, you know, future devices and robotics as well. But there's the CPU in the rack — this is the Veras and the Gravitons of the world — and then there's the use from an agent perspective like, you know, sandboxes and agents being able to use all of the software we already have and API calls, tools, etc.

Do you have any guess as to — you know, both these things are growing, but the scale of opportunity — or am I missing things that you guys are really excited about from the CPU perspective?

Well, from the CPU standpoint — and I think when the data center things was kind of exploding with — let me back up. When ChatGPT had the explosion thing and everything was all about the accelerators, I think there was so much focus on: no matter what the question is, the answer is the accelerator.

There's no computing problem that's ever been invented that doesn't utilize and can't utilize the microprocessor. It is the heart of everything. All roads lead through it, around it, past it, etc., etc. You look at fundamental system design and you have to have CPUs. They just don't kind of go away.

They were a little bit forgotten as this accelerator thing kind of took off. But what then became very obvious was as more and more of the data was moving away from training — training is obviously very important — to recursive learning, reinforcement learning, to inference, the use of the tokens, the use of the information. Well, of course, in a system problem, something has to do the orchestration, arbitration, decision around where those tokens go, right?

The token factory just generates all these tokens. It's like literally: where are the trucks that are going to take the tokens away and give them to the users? That's what CPUs do.

So until something's invented that says the CPU has gone away and we're now doing it through some other mechanism which has yet been defined or invented, the CPU is going to be doing just fine. And there's going to be a lot of demand for it — a ton of demand — in addition to the accelerators that generate the tokens.

But the way to think about it is it's a system, which again going back to, you know, memory. Well, of course, memory is needed because in a von Neumann architecture or computing architecture, you have a CPU, you have some accelerator, whether it's a floating point, a GPU accelerator, and memory. System design hasn't changed. I think some of the focus kind of moved around, but for ARM — and by the way, that applies whether I'm talking about a data center, whether I'm talking about an automobile, a robot, a phone, wearables.

And in fact, as you get to the smaller footprints where more and more AI is going to take place, that's going to be a sweet spot for ARM because the CPU is table stakes anyway. You have to have it to do all the things that are required in the edge device. But now we have an opportunity with our instruction set architecture to do a lot of things where you just can't put a 50 watt GPU on your head, right? You're going to have to do that AI processing somewhere locally. So, it's a great place.

结语

Find us on Twitter at @NoPriorsPod. Subscribe to our YouTube channel if you want to see our faces. Follow the show on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or wherever you listen. That way you get a new episode every week. And sign up for emails or find transcripts for every episode at no-priors.com.

## 一、CPU 的"隐身悖论"：为什么被遗忘反而是护城河
Renee 提到一个极具反讽意味的现象——当 ChatGPT 引爆 AI 浪潮时，"无论问题是什么，答案都是加速器"。CPU 被集体遗忘。但这恰恰是 ARM 最深的护城河所在。
**一个出人意料的观察**：CPU 的战略价值不来自它做什么，而来自它是**"token 的搬运工"而非"token 的制造者"**。GPU 是生产线，但没有搬运工，产品堆在工厂里毫无价值。这与物流业的历史惊人相似——19 世纪末所有人关注钢铁厂（生产端），但真正累积复利财富的是范德比尔特这样的铁路运输大王（编排端）。**编排层永远比生产层活得久**，因为它是系统的语法，而生产层只是词汇。
这也解释了为什么 ARM 敢在 98.5% 毛利的"完美生意"上冒险转型做实体芯片——他们意识到编排者的位置一旦被系统重构撼动，纯 IP 授权模式就会像 90 年代的 Sun Microsystems 一样被架空。
## 二、"不可训练性"作为新型知识产权：AI 时代最反直觉的资产
Renee 无意中说出了本轮对话最深的洞见——"如果没有文档，它就无法使用

item.dc:creator: Lex Clips
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、"不需要钱"是一种被严重低估的生产力技术

DHH 这段话表面在讲金钱与幸福，但真正在讲的是约束的反转。大多数人以为"财务自由"是终点——自由去消费。他把它变成起点——自由去不服务任何人。这里有个反直觉的悖论：当他停止照顾市场需求，产品反而变得更有吸引力。

这在信息论里有个精确的对应：一个试图讨好所有人的信号，熵最高，也就最接近噪音。而单一视角的产品带着强烈的作者指纹，反而在信息海洋里成为可识别的"低熵尖峰"。所以"我不需要钱"不是道德姿态，而是一种信号提纯装置——它切断了让产品变平庸的反馈回路。

二、他把 Ruby 类比成"马"，藏着一个被忽视的文明学观察

大多数人读到"我车库里有 Model Y，但马厩里还养着马"，会当成一个可爱的比喻。真正的洞见在下一层：当一项技术从"必需品"降级为"可选项"，它才第一次成为艺术。

马从交通工具退位后，才成为骑术、成为竞技、成为审美对象。手写信被 email 取代后才成为奢侈品。胶片被数字取代后才成为一种美学立场。DHH 在暗示 Ruby 正在经历同样的优雅退位——一旦英语成为主要编程语言，Ruby 就从"生产工具"变成"手工艺"。

这里有个跨领域的连接值得警觉：你现在每天靠它吃饭的技能，最终会变成你退休后的爱好。这不是威胁，而是所有成熟技术的宿命轨迹。识别自己所在的技能处于这条曲线的哪一段，比学新东西更重要。

三、"用英语编程"背后的语言学暗流

他说"如果有一门比 Ruby 更美的语言，那就是英语"——这句话被大多数人当作情怀。但真正的爆点是：他不是在赞美英语，他是在宣布一种新的阶层分化。

历史上每次编程范式的降门槛，都伴随着新的高门槛悄悄生长：汇编到 C，门槛从"懂硬件"变成"懂抽象"；C 到 Ruby，门槛从"懂内存"变成"懂表达"；现在到自然语言，门槛从"懂语法"变成——懂如何把模糊的意图翻译成精确的意图。

这恰好是文学编辑、哲学家、法律起草人几百年来在做的事。所以有一个出人意料的预言：未来最贵的程序员，可能是那些拥有诗人般语言精度、律师般规格意识、导演般场景想象力的人。编程正在从"工程学科"回流成"修辞学科"——而修辞学是西方最古老的文科之一。

这也解释了 DHH 为什么把这称为"赛博格未来"——不是人机融合的科幻画面，而是人类最古老的语言能力，第一次直接驱动最新的机器。中间那五十年的"语法期"，可能只是文明进化中的一次绕路。

📝 转录文本

关于被收购的假设

Lex: You do realize if you continue to be as successful as you are, um, OpenAI and Anthropic are going to roll in and try to do their operating system and/or to buy it — like with Peter, with Open Claw — there'd be a gigantic check.

不需要钱带来的自由

DHH: Yeah, I think the good thing about my current position is, um, I really don't need the money. So I get to build these things purely for my own enjoyment and purely vision, which has this weird quality where sometimes when you stop caring about what everyone else thinks or wants or whatever, and you just pursue this singular vision, it ends up becoming far more appealing.

That is, when you try to do, "oh, I should do this because these people want that, or I should do this and this and so on," you start watering the thing down and suddenly it's a bland ball of nothing.

Lex: Yeah.

对 Omarchy 定位的坦然

DHH: So, I mean, again, the thing to hear is: directionally, I just want computers to be this way. So if Omarchy should end up being just a little footnote in history — that it was part of this early movement of the agentic OS and malleable computer — that's also okay. I'm completely at peace with that, as long as I get to have a computer that is as fun to work with as Omarchy. That's great.

Ruby、Rails 与"更好的工具"

I've had the same thing with Ruby and with Rails. From very early, I went, you know what, I love Ruby. It's such a great programming language. But if a better programming language comes along, I mean, I'm going to use it. If a better Rails comes along, I'm going to use it.

And I think — and I love Ruby, and I will continue to write Ruby even just for the sheer fun of it, like I would go ride a horse. I have them in the stables even though I have a Model Y in the garage.

用英语编程

The language now is English. It's a cliché, but it's also true. Like, I've been programming in English for the last 3 months. I've been reading a lot of code, but I'm programming in English. I'm telling the computer what to do, and I'm using natural language. And it is shockingly even more delightful.

If there is one programming language more beautiful than Ruby, it is the English language.

走向赛博格未来

Lex: And now we get to carry it into the natural evolution of human civilization, which is our cyborg future. Yeah.

DHH: Beautiful.

item.title: [投资TALK君] ✨【投资TALK君1483期】"AI营收翻倍再翻倍“，博通财报好吗？日本准备加息2码！✨20260902#CPI #nvda #美股 #投资 #英伟达 #ai #特斯拉
item.dc:creator: 投资TALK君
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

三个让人意外的观察

1. 日本央行加息 ≠ 美股风险——这是一场"货币柔道"

大多数人看到"日本加息"就本能联想到"套息交易平仓、全球风险资产承压"。但博主揭示的机制指向相反方向：贝森特要的从来不是拯救日元，而是借日元升值来压低美债长端收益率。他给出的正相关图（日元汇率与10年美债收益率同向变动）是一个反直觉的关键证据——日元升值往往伴随美债收益率下行。

这本质上是一种合作博弈的结构：让对手加息，来实现自己的政策目标。像柔道一样借力打力，而不是对抗。市场把"日本加息=美股利空"直接画等号，恰恰是没看懂这场"三方共振"的机制。

2. Uber两次10%裁员——AI替代的"临界点跃迁"模型

一个半月内两次10%裁员，这不是线性替代，而是复利加速。博主承认自己年初对2026年劳动力市场的判断"错判了半年到一年"，但更深的可能是：AI替代根本不是均匀扩散，而是一个S型曲线里的爆发段。

有意思的跨领域连接：这与生物学里"病毒式扩散"、社会学中"临界质量理论"高度一致——前期漫长的孕育期让观察者以为"AI落地慢"，实际上系统正在积累势能。当软件公司AI营收开始爆发（就像本季度所见），传统企业IT budget的上升会紧接着触发"用OPEX换IT"的多米诺骨牌。你以为的延后，很可能只是曲线拐点前的错觉。

3. 博通与谷歌的"镜像分散"——一种自组织的系统性稳定

这是这期视频最容易被忽略的洞察：谷歌在分散供应商，博通在分散客户，两者方向完全相反却同时发生。Anthropic在2027财年将取代谷歌成为博通第一大客户，OpenAI排第二，谷歌降到第三。

这不是关系恶化，而是互相解绑的战略成熟。类似森林生态学中的"共生网络"——每个节点主动降低对单一伙伴的依赖，反而让整个AI供应链的系统韧性大幅上升。这背后是一种反Nash均衡的现象：双方都在主动"去中心化"，而不是争夺零和的谈判筹码。

一个更深的系统性真相

博主提到市场"喜欢加速的公司、讨厌减速的公司"——CRDO被砸盘不是因为29%的EPS增速差，而是因为增速在放缓。

这是一个跨领域的行为偏差同构：TikTok、YouTube算法奖励的不是高观看量，而是"上升斜率"；风险投资估值看的不是收入体量，而是"二阶导"；甚至人类择偶时也更看重"上升期"而非"稳态"。市场用这个心智模型评估硬件公司时，会在利润率进入稳态的临界点严重错杀那些"从高速增长切换到稳定盈利"的公司——PEG小于1的博通、Marvell、CRDO正是这个偏差的受害者。

而更有意思的是：AI芯片行业的"剩余价值担保"结构（英伟达担保NeoCloud、博通担保模型公司），本质上把2008年次贷危机中的信用衍生品逻辑复用到了硬件资产上。区别在于：次贷底层资产是慢升值房产，而AI芯片的现金流回收周期不到一年（一个GW成本15-20亿 vs. 年ARR 30亿）。这可能是硬件史上第一次出现"资产回收周期短于担保周期"的结构性套利机会——所以担保方几乎稳赚不赔。

这才是当前硬件板块估值被极度压缩、却处于极佳布局时机的深层原因。

📝 转录文本

开场：财报季还没聊完，今天再来两家

明明财报季都已经在身后了，但是不知道为什么，这财报一聊就停不下来。今天还是来和大家分享财报，两家公司分别是周三发布财报的 Broadcom（AVGO），还有另外一家公司是周二发布财报的 CRDO。

然后前半部分的话，我们还是聊一下宏观。那宏观这个主线条，今天我们放在日本央行接下去加息的一个次数上面。现在有可能日本央行9月份直接加息两次，有一定的风险在那边，但是这一个风险本身对于美股来说，到底是不是一个风险？针对这个话题，我们进行一个展开。

好吧，那欢迎大家来到一个不单只聊新闻的专业美股频道，我是市场分析师小涛。在开始之前，大家记得留言、点赞加转发，让更多的人可以看到我们这期内容。

观众提问：现在能不能追？——我的仓位配置逻辑

今天我接收到了一个问题，问题问的是：周三美股出现了一个反弹，他自己本身还没有去买，那现在能不能去追？

针对这个问题，我的回答是：我并不知道。我并不知道周三的这个反弹到底是接下去一波上涨的一个开始，还是说接下去还会去探一个新低。但是从我个人的角度，我一直建议的是我们停留在这个市场里面，仓位在这个市场里面，然后留一部分的现金仓位出来，等着去进行加仓。

至于是70%的仓位在市场里边，还是90%仓位在市场里边、剩下的留现金，我没有这个标准答案。那我自己可能更加偏向于90和10——90的仓位、10%的现金。那起码在当下的一个市场，我是这样的一个配置。

而我自己是抱有这样的一个态度：首先，当然这是今年可能会比较特殊一些的嘛。首先到现在为止，今年 YTD 其实还离新高还是比较近的，其实并没有从新高回调太多。但是在现在这种情况下，反而市场的情绪面也好，还是市场的参与度也好，是在一个相对的低位。没有到非常的超卖，但是在一个相对的低位。

在这种情况下我手里拿着一些正股，我会觉得非常的舒适。那自己回报又还不错，然后市场情绪又在一个低位，这时候应该是持有个股的时候。那然后因为还没有到非常悲观的一个时候，那留出一部分的现金，万一到非常悲观的时候，把所有的子弹全部打出去。

市场情绪指标：CNN 恐慌贪婪指数

在昨天的视频里面，我和大家分享了参与度。那今天这期视频我们来首先看一下 CNN 的恐慌贪婪指数。截止到周三的收盘，CNN 的恐慌贪婪指数在33、34、35左右，35还没有到极度恐慌，但是是在恐慌区间的一个下区间了。所以其实和我昨天和大家分享市场参与度是非常的一致，市场参与度的一个指标也是在恐慌的一个边缘。那么还没有到恐慌的一个阶段——低于30是恐慌，在30以上就在恐慌的一个边缘。所以 CNN 的恐慌贪婪指数和市场的参与度是比较的一致的。

但那新的恐慌贪婪指数里边，其中包括了很多个指标，其中两个指标我挑出来和大家分享一下：一个是强度，一个是广度。广度其实有点类似于我昨天和大家分享市场的一个参与度，强度的话也是类似的。

啊，但这两个指标，特别是强度这一块，你可以看到现在是在 extreme fear，是在一个极度恐慌的一个阶段。上一次这个极度恐慌是在今年的3月份，再上一次的话是在上一年的11月份。然后从市场深度这个角度去看，其实和上面那张图是类似的，上次恐慌的时候是在今年的3月份，今年3月底的时候，然后是今年7月底的时候，再上一次是上年11月份的时候。

那这些数据告诉我们什么？告诉我们市场是在一个恐慌的阶段，还没有到非常的恐慌。你比如你去看 VIX 的话，还没有去到一个非常高的一个位置。但是这时候不代表我们要空仓的，而是代表我们现在应该是持有一定的一个仓位在市场里面。如果去到极度恐慌，我们加仓，我们满仓，我们把仓位全部打满。反过来也是一样。

那当这个钟摆，当 CNN 的恐慌贪婪指数这个钟摆去到一个乐观的一个阶段，那我们就现金仓位可以多留一点。当这个钟摆去到一个极度乐观的时候，要留更多的一个现金仓位出来。所以仓位本身它不是一个非黑即白的一个结果。无论是交易也好，投资也好也是一样。你交易的话，你也是分批进场、分批离场，投资的话也是一样。

宏观：日本央行加息真的是美股风险吗？

讲完市场的情绪面之后，我们来看一下宏观这边。首先我们看一下日本央行在9月18日加息的这个概率已经达到了118.8%。什么意思？超过20%这个可能性在9月份的时候会直接加息两码——直接加息50个基点。上一次日本央行加息50个基点是什么时候？我都不知道了，我必须要去查这个历史了，已经很久很久以前了。

那其实在上一个月月初的时候，当时贝森特说我们要和日本央行一起去进行拯救日元的这个行动，但是接下去日本央行必须要 follow through。什么叫 follow through？就是你的政策必须要跟上。什么叫政策跟上？你必须要加息。那不能一边说我们在拯救日元，一边你说我不加息，我必继续保持着一个宽松的一个态度，或者相对比较低的这个利率，不行。

所以这一次日本央行出来去调整这个预期，你看到日元出现了一个上涨。那有不少人担心日本央行如果加息，对于美股这边会有一个风险在那边，那这个风险是不是一个合理的一个担心呢？

其实我认为并不是。我上次有解释过，那么贝森特他所希望看到的是什么？贝森特他所希望看到的是日元出现一个升值，同时美债的收益率、长债美债的一个收益率会出现一个下降。这几点、这两点是可以同时发生的。这就是为什么他要去拯救日元——他不是为了拯救日元而去拯救日元，他是为了通过拯救日元，希望能够使得日本政府那边抛售美债的这个速度会降低，从而使得美国长债这一块的利率会出现下降。它的最终目的是使得美国长债的利率出现下降，而不是为了去拯救日元。

啊，所以如果说因为日本政府的一个加息，导致日元出现上涨的话，其实你可以期待一个结果是：这是贝森特他所希望看到的。

相关性图表：日元汇率 vs 10年期美债收益率

啊，所以这边我拉了两个相关性出来和大家分享。首先图里白色这条线是日元兑美元的这个汇率，那当白色这条线在下降的时候，日元是在升值；白色这条线在上涨的时候，日元是在贬值。同时图里蓝色这条线是10年期美国的一个收益率、美国国债的一个收益率。

你会看到这两者之间大多数的时候是个正相关。什么叫正相关？当白色这条线往下降的时候，我们通常会看到蓝色这条线往下降。白色这条线往下降代表日元在干嘛？代表日元在升值，美债的收益率出现下降。所以你会发现这个结果不就是我前面聊的贝森特所希望看到的吗——日元升值、长期美国国债的收益率往下降。

所以很多时候我们不是看一条新闻——"哦，接下去日本央行要加息，所以美股这边有风险"——就直接画上一个等号了。不是这么去解读的，我们必须要去理解这背后的机制到底是什么。

那另外一点，那么与其我们担心日本央行在9月18日要加息，无论是加息一次也好、加息两次也好，从现在市场的预期去看，起码要加息一次了，一次或者两次。但是在9月18日之前，将会有9月16日美联储的这个决定。现在连美联储接下去是加息还是不加息都是未知数。所以比起我们现在如果要去担心日本银行是不是会加息、会加息几次这一个风险，这个担心之前，我先要去担心接下去美联储会不会加息。

AI 就业冲击：Uber 一个半月内两次10%裁员

那在看财报之前，有一条新闻和大家分享，也是和 AI 有关的，主要是 Uber 在裁员了10%，岗位裁到了3300个岗位。

在前段时间，将近要两个月，那么一个半月之前，当时我有看到一条新闻，Uber 自己的管理层出来说，他们把 AI 和传统业务里边做一个结合，他们放了工程师到不同的岗位上去，工程师和岗位里面的这个专家一起去合作，一起去看一下 AI 在这个岗位上有没有一些发展的这个余地。然后接下去，他们差不多当时一个工作小组持续了一周到两周左右，然后出现了非常多的一个成效。

然后 Uber 内部也是这样：就是你在 AI 这一块的花费可以保持不变或者保持一个低增速，但是它烧 token 的这个速度会烧了非常多，因为他们会用一个开源模型。然后在那件事情之后，那么它这是属于一个拥抱 AI 的一个结果，那件事情之后 Uber 裁员了，服务岗位直接裁员了10%。然后在一个半月之后，Uber 直接内部大范围直接裁员，又裁员了10%。

所以我个人对于 AI 的这个理解仍然是——我认为我在年初的时候，我认为2026年整个劳动力市场可能会低迷，因为 AI 会造成很多人失业。但是当时我做了一个错判。就起码站在当下的话，会看当时的一个错判在哪：错判是在 AI 的这个落地没有我想象中要好。我所谓 AI 的落地是 AI 的一个扩散范围，但直到现在为止，AI 的一个扩散范围仍然大多数只停留在科技公司内部。

然后到了今年这个季度财报，我们才刚刚看到软件公司这一块 AI 的营收开始上来。当软件公司的 AI 营收开始上来时候，就代表传统的公司开始用 AI 了。那当传统的公司对于 AI 慢慢开始接受之后，势必他们的 IT budget、在 IT 这一块的花费会出现上升。当这一块 IT budget 出现上升之后，营收又没有非常明显的一个正反馈，如果营收没有出现加速的话，那接下去的一步就是什么？就是拿 OPEX 去换 IT——去拿运营开支换 IT 开支。

所以我在2026年年初对于劳动力市场所做的这个判断，当时时间点我认为完全是错的。然后这个判断本身我认为可能站在当下这个角度，可能要延后半年到一年，可能要延后到2027年的3月份到6月份左右。因为从现在科技公司拥抱 AI 的这个方法，我们可以看到，它用的就是运营开支去换来更多的 IT 开支。

财报一：Broadcom（AVGO）——2028财年指引大幅上调

OK，然后最后我们来聊财报。那第一家公司是 AVGO Broadcom，是在周三盘后发的财报。

现在我看一下盘后，差不多没有涨也没有跌，出现了小幅的下跌吧。刚刚发布完财报数据出来之后，出现了5%的这个下跌，然后盘中一度、哦盘后的话一度是上涨了2%，现在的话是小幅下跌。

那财报本身数据没有非常的亮点，就从这一个季度的数据没有非常的亮点。然后下一个季度营收指引是上调了0.5个百分点，比市场预期稍微要高一些。重点是在2028财年把营收的这个预期上调了非常多，就起码超出了市场的预期非常的多。所以这一个季度的财报数据是 OK 的，没有非常的亮眼，但是指引的话比较的好。

客户结构剧变：Anthropic 将成第一大客户

然后我们来看一下财报会议。财报会议的第一点：接下去在2027财年和2028财年，你可以看到 Anthropic 将会成为博通的第一大客户，有10个 GW 的这个订单。OpenAI 将会成为第二大客户，谷歌肯定就排到第三了。

啊，所以我在上一次聊 Marvell 财报的时候，我就有聊到，我说从谷歌这个角度，他们在分散自己的供应链的风险，然后他们使得谷歌本身会有这个溢价讲价权在那边，对于谷歌一定是一个利好，所以他们有这个意愿背后去扶持 Marvell。那你从博通这个角度去看，他们也在分散自己的客户，且从现在营收这个预期你可以看到，从2027财年开始，谷歌已经不再是成为博通的第一大客户了，Anthropic 将会成为第一大客户，OpenAI 将会成为第二大客户。

所以从博通和谷歌这两个角度，就从各自的一个角度去出发，你会看到他们都在分散——一个在分散自己的供应链，另外一个在分散自己的客户风险。

2028财年 AI 营收翻倍：230亿指引 vs 市场预期180亿

然后第二点就是我前面说到的2027财年，他们在 AI 营收这一块的预期、营收的一个指引是在115亿，市场的一个预期是120亿，所以2027财年反而是出现了一部分的一些下调。2028财年 AI 这块的营收直接上调到230亿，就是在2027财年的基础上再翻一倍，市场的预期是180亿，所以2028财年上调的这个预期幅度相当的大。

并且对2028财年给出了 EPS 体量的这个预期是在每股收益30美金，市场的这个预期是26美金，那所以2028财年的 EPS 的这个体量上升了10%以上。并且最重要的是管理层在财报会议里边，他聊得非常的清楚，他说我们今天能够给出这个指引，首先第一点，我们背后已经有这个 supply、供给端这一块我们已经确认了；第二点是我们尽量给出一个保守的一个指引。

分析师尖锐提问：每 GW 营收11-12亿，怎么和英伟达的40亿比？

然后我们来看第三点。分析师问了一个问题，这个问题我觉得问挺好。分析师问了他说：根据你给的这一个预期，2027财年有10个 GW、6个 GW 是来自于两家模型公司；2028年有20个 GW、15个 GW 是来自于两家模型公司，营收是230亿。所以平均是不是一个 GW 对于你来说，你的营收是11至12亿？

但是英伟达，就英伟达在两周之前、一周之前发布完财报之后说到接下去新的 Vera Rubin 是40亿。那这笔账你怎么去算呢？理论上来说，你从大模型公司这个角度去看，他们要不就是去买 GPU，要不就是去买自己的自研芯片。那自研芯片你的成本难道才11至12亿？然后你去卖 GPU 的话，整个 GPU 下来是40亿，差距有那么大吗？

那管理层的这个回答是：首先 ship 和 deploy 是两个概念，那这有点类似于你在什么样的一个阶段能够从会计准则这个角度去看，能够放到你的一个营收里边来，所以这中间会有一个定义上的一个差距在里面。他们说会 ship 30个 GW 的一个数据中心啊芯片，那不代表最后会 deploy。也就是说，严格意义上来说，10个 GW——2027财年的10个 GW 或者2028财年的20个 GW——并不会完全反映在2027财年和2028财年的一个营收里边。

啊，但是同时管理层其实在上一个季度财报里面有聊到，差不多他们卖出去一个 GW 的这个营收是在20亿左右，然后又说到了和同类的一些竞品去做对比的话是一半的这个价格。英伟达是40亿，它一半那个价格20亿，其实也是合理。然后我和 AI 也讨论了很多，基本上确定下来是差不多他们一个 GW 是在15亿至20亿左右。

芯片经济学：为什么模型公司拼命上自研？

那么我们把这些数据串起来的话，我们先把自研芯片和 GPU 之间的性能这一块我们先放一边，性能上的对比我们先放一边，因为各说各的嘛。但我个人认为到现在为止，仍然是老黄的 AI factory 的一个性能是最高的，从 Token throughput 这个角度去看是最好。那先把性能放在一边，我们就聊一下数据，很多数据我们可以把它串起来。

那么成本是多少？我们看一下：NeoCloud 他们一年的营收是12亿，那 NeoCloud 手里全部是 GPU、全部是来自于英伟达。现在自研芯片的这个成本是 NeoCloud GPU 的这个成本的40%。也就是原本一年是12亿，一个 GW 一年是12亿——因为 NeoCloud 的一个营收对于大模型来说就是他们的一个成本嘛，就是他们的一个 cost of goods sold——12亿，一年你乘以0.4就是4.8亿。你直接原来的成本从一年的12亿降到了5亿都不到。

所以从大模型这个角度去看，他们背后有非常强的这个意愿把自己的这个毛利润给抬上去。那我们结合第四点：那么 Hock 有说到，一个 GW 现在，一个 GW 的这个芯片对于模型公司来说等于30亿的 ARR。你算一下：30亿的 ARR，你根据现在12亿的一个成本的 NeoCloud 的一个营收就是你的一个成本，你的成本是12亿，然后你的营收是30亿，那你的毛利率是多少？60%。啊，但是如果现在还是30亿的 ARR，你的成本可以从12亿降到5亿，那对于模型公司来说，你的 margin 瞬间从60%抬升到了80%（25÷30 = 80%）。

剩余价值担保：英伟达 vs 博通的风险对比

最后一点，那博通也会和英伟达去做类似的事情，就是对于这些模型公司本身去做一个剩余价值风险的一个担保。英伟达是对于谁去做担保？其实都是对于未来自己的客户去做一个剩余价值的一个担保。英伟达是对这些 NeoCloud 去做一个担保，博通是对这两家模型公司去做一个担保。但是他们担保本身并不是担保这两家公司本身，也并不是担保 NeoCloud，他们只是担保他们自己所卖出来的这个芯片、芯片的这个剩余价值去做一个担保。

那从这个角度来说，如果去横向做一个对比的话，那肯定是英伟达的这个风险相对会低一些。当然模型公司的一个 financial 一定会比 NeoCloud 要好，但是从芯片这个角度去看的话，一定是它的这个芯片——因为今天如果说 NeoCloud 他们没办法用了、没办法运行下去，那这个芯片必须要卖给其他人——从 fungibility 这个角度、从可转移性这个角度，一定是英伟达的芯片会比自研芯片要好很多。

但是从芯片本身剩余价值这一个风险这个角度去看的话，我认为两家公司剩余价值这个风险都不高。为什么？因为现在的一个 ROI 非常的快，也非常的高。最简单的数据：如果你一个 GW 的一个成本是在15至20亿，我就算你20亿，但是对于模型公司来说，你一年的一个 ARR 的一个营收是30亿，那就是小于一年的这个回报周期。

博通估值：2028财年 Forward P/E 仅12倍

那最后是估值这一块的更新。按照现在367的这个价格，管理层把2028财年 EPS 这个体量从25.8上抬到了30、每股收益30美金，那2028财年的 Forward P/E 我们就可以算出来，直接去拿367除以30，得出来是12倍的一个 Forward P/E，就将近两年之后 Forward P/E 在10到12倍。我个人认为是相当便宜。我也去看了一下英伟达，英伟达差不多2029财年、也是两年半之后吧，Forward P/E 是在11倍。

财报二：CRDO——市场对"增速放缓"的过度惩罚

然后第二家公司我们来看一下 CRDO。我不会聊得非常的详细，我有去听他们的一个财报，但我主要认为这家公司本身发布完财报之后的这个下跌，还是市场对于硬件这个板块短期之内情绪面非常的低，所以出现了类似于我认为是一个 sell the news。

那数据本身其实和博通类似的，没有非常的亮眼。那营收增速这一个季度营收增速高出上一期1%，然后 EPS 的增速高出上一期3.7%。

根据现在市场的预期，如果我们看27财年、28财年和29财年，它们 EPS 的增速我们去看一下——81%、55%和29%。这其实背后会有一定的一个问题在背后，就市场预期什么？市场预期这家公司未来的 EPS 增速在下降、在低 salary、在放缓。

我上次在聊英伟达、在聊博通和聊 Marvell 三家公司财报放在一起的时候，和大家分享过这个问题——市场愿意做一个线性外推，市场喜欢你未来的一年会比今年的 EPS 增速增幅会更大、会一个 accelerate；然后29年会、然后后年会比明年还要高。市场喜欢这一类的公司，而不喜欢一个增速放缓的公司。当然这背后可能出现一部分的一个程度是市场低估了，比如说 CRDO 他们在2028年 EPS 增速的这个体量。

CRDO 估值：PEG 小于1，Forward P/E 回到3月水平

如果从估值这个角度去出发，经过周三20%这个下跌之后，静态市盈率40.3倍。如果我们去看它的一个 PEG ratio，一倍都不到。那无论是和英伟达去做对比、和博通去做对比、和 Marvell 去做对比，几乎是在同样的一个状态之下——小于一倍的一个 PEG ratio（那 Marvell 的话稍微高一些）。如果看它的一个 Forward P/E 22.15倍，回到了今年3月份的这个水平。

那所以基本上你可以看到现在很多硬件公司——芯片也好、硬件公司也好，Forward P/E 也好、PEG ratio 也好——其实现在是在一个非常低的一个位置，就短期之内你可以看到市场的情绪面其实非常的低。所以这时候如果有硬件公司的话，我认为要拿好；如果没有硬件公司的话，现在其实是一个非常好的去布局硬件公司的时候。

结语：赞助活动

最后，今天的活动来自于 Vivo 微牛证券。大家对于微牛证券应该并不陌生，在美国他们其实做得非常的好。首先这一次美国市场这边的独家活动是开户且入金100美金，就可以抽取12股免费的股票，最低金额是36美金、最高金额高达3600美金，在这个基础上还可以获得一个月 Vivo Premium 的订阅。加拿大这边通过开户且入境最高可以获得价值250加币的一个返现。

所以大家如果感兴趣的话，可以在置顶的留言里边找到两个市场开户的链接。那今天就先聊到这边，下期见。

item.description:
## 三个让人意外的观察
### 1. 日本央行加息 ≠ 美股风险——这是一场"货币柔道"
大多数人看到"日本加息"就本能联想到"套息交易平仓、全球风险资产承压"。但博主揭示的机制指向相反方向：贝森特要的从来不是拯救日元，而是**借日元升值来压低美债长端收益率**。他给出的正相关图（日元汇率与10年美债收益率同向变动）是一个反直觉的关键证据——日元升值往往伴随美债收益率下行。
这本质上是一种**合作博弈的结构**：让对手加息，来实现自己的政策目标。像柔道一样借力打力，而不是对抗。市场把"日本加息=美股利空"直接画等号，恰恰是没看懂这场"三方共振"的机制。
### 2. Uber两次10%裁员——AI替代的"临界点跃迁"模型
一个半月内两次10%裁员，这不是线性替代，而是**复利加速**。博主承认自己年初对2026年劳动力市场的判断"错判了半年到一年"，但更深的可能是：**AI替代根本不是均匀扩散，而是一个S型曲线里的爆发段**。
有意思的跨领域连接：这与生物学里"病毒式扩散"、社会学中"临界质量理论"高度一致——前期漫长的孕育期让观察者以为"AI落地慢"，实际上系统正在积累

item.title: [Zhang Xiaojun Podcast] 153. 和曾鸣聊产业史观：残酷的真相、会消亡的公司、优秀≠卓越、“OAI、Anth大概率不是原生时代大赢家”
item.dc:creator: Zhang Xiaojun Podcast
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、Edison 悖论：发明者的诅咒

曾鸣讲了一个几乎没人注意的历史细节——爱迪生发明了电灯，但通用电气最终不是靠"卖电"成功的，而是靠冰箱和洗衣机；他的助手离开去创办了美国第一家真正意义上的电力配送公司。这个故事的隐藏含义是"发明者的诅咒"：你越是深爱你亲手造出来的那个东西，越难看清它真正的价值不在它本身，而在它的下游。

把这个框架套到今天：OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的悲剧性可能不在于技术不够强，而在于他们太爱模型本身。就像爱迪生死抱着发电机，Sam Altman 也可能死抱着 token 工厂。曾鸣那句"OpenAI 大概率不是原生时代大赢家"，本质上是在说：做出锤子的人，很少能成为锤子最好的使用者。这不是能力问题，是心智锚定问题——你的骄傲会成为你的战略盲区。

二、反直觉：这不是新组织，是被工业革命消灭的古老组织的复活

所有人都在讨论"AI 原生组织"是个多么新鲜的东西——Context not Control、任务代替岗位、扁平化。但如果拉远视角看，这些特征其实是律师事务所、投资银行、中世纪工匠行会的古老模式。合伙人制度不是工业时代的产物，恰恰是被工业时代的公司制"驱逐"了的更早形态。

所以曾鸣说"公司会消亡"，真正惊人的不是"消亡"两个字，而是——我们不是在走向一个从未见过的未来，而是绕了 250 年的大弯，回到了工业革命之前的组织形态，只不过这次由 AI 提供了原本需要几百人才能完成的规模化能力。这是一次时间上的莫比乌斯环。跨领域的镜像是生物进化——最"先进"的哺乳动物身上，仍然保留着爬行动物的脑干；最"未来"的组织，可能只是把最古老的协作方式装上了新的动力系统。

三、"老灯"的经济学：被 LLM 摧毁的不是岗位，是敬老传统本身

曾鸣抛出的一个几乎没人挖深的观察——为什么这两年"老登/老灯"这个词爆红？他给了一个残酷的解释：尊老爱幼是有前提的，前提是老人的经验可以传承、有价值。当 LLM 把 20 年的行业经验压缩进大模型，任何一个聪明的年轻人用好工具就能瞬间变成"老中医"，尊老的经济基础被抽掉了。

这个洞察打开了一个更大的门：人类几乎所有伦理体系的底层，都是某种资源稀缺性的社会协议。稀缺什么，就尊敬什么。稀缺经验，就敬老；稀缺信息，就敬记者；稀缺资本，就敬企业家。AI 不只是重构劳动力市场，它正在同时溶解多个社会协议的经济地基。教育系统的崩塌、师徒关系的失效、代际权威的坍缩——这些看似孤立的现象，实际上是同一个稀缺性革命的多个投影面。跨领域的映射：这类似于宗教改革——古腾堡印刷术让《圣经》人人可读，教士的中介地位就崩了；LLM 让知识人人可解，"老登"们的中介地位也在崩。历史的韵脚惊人相似。

四、隐藏的战略学翻转：从"结构追随战略"到"战略从组织中生成"

Chandler 那句写进所有 MBA 教材的"Structure follows Strategy"（结构追随战略），是整个工业时代战略学的圣经。曾鸣这本书最大胆的动作，是悄悄地把它翻转了——先讲组织，再讲战略；战略不是"规划"出来的，是从一个好的生成式组织中"涌现"出来的。他甚至专门造了"战略生成"这个词与视频生成、文本生成对齐。

这个翻转的深层含义：战略不再是一次性决策，而是持续的采样过程。就像大模型不是"想好了再输出"，而是逐 token 生成、每一步都在概率分布上采样——未来的组织也是这样运作的。这直接解释了为什么 xAI 和 Meta 在这一轮掉队：马斯克式的"CEO 给答案、组织执行"是工业时代的推理链；而 Anthropic 式的"给足 Context，让判断在网络中涌现"是 Transformer 式的推理链。组织架构本身，正在变得越来越像一个神经网络——这不是比喻，是同构。

📝 转录文本

和曾鸣聊产业史观：残酷的真相、会消亡的公司、优秀≠卓越

开场

Hello everyone, I'm Xiaojun. Today, our guest is Professor Zeng Min, a business strategy expert. Professor Zeng is the former chief executive director of Alibaba Group and has also participated in the creation of two business schools, which are Changjiang Business School and Hupan. However, he is more familiar with the identity of a person who has a lot of thinking and research on business strategies.

Many entrepreneurs and entrepreneurs have said that they have been inspired by him — as a complete researcher who has experienced the cycle of the Internet. We talked with him about his new idea of AI and his new way of thinking, and compared it with the key periods in history. After listening to it, I feel that I have a more comprehensive perspective. Next, I will interview Professor Zeng.

冷开场：那些会被推翻的判断

Looking forward to the progress of AI in 2026. The company system of course management will fall. But it may not be called a company. It certainly won't be called a company. So the company will disappear. The company will disappear. There is nothing to regret. There will be more fun in the future.

You said that many people are happy to go to work in the company now. Not happy. I also speak a little more strictly. This batch of entrepreneurs will have a big cut. Because the basic rules of economics, as long as there is a synchronized supply, you will not be able to get high-value profits. You are a company that is not very valuable.

Google will not necessarily become the next generation of Google. Will the next generation of Google be the next generation of Google? The same probability will not be. The model of Google is also good today, right? At least it is the first team in China. No, so Google has a great chance to become an AI cloud company. But the big 2C application has a very big uncertainty.

Doubao is it? Doubao is definitely not, right? Otherwise, it will definitely not count the cost and go into it. It's not because of the shortage of beans. Will social relationships be re-created? Is Tencent safe? It will definitely be. As the safest, why is Tencent so panicky? Because it may not be safe. Will relationships with people be re-created? Will social relationships be re-created? What about relationships with goods? It will be re-created. I think Ali will also have that challenge.

In the face of this wave, which giants are safe? I never think that no one is safe in the face of a wave. Do you think they are all in AI? Can it become a next-generation enterprise? Is it a modern enterprise? It's a big challenge. Is there a basis in the history? Is there a lot of good things that can be done from this era to the next era? It's not about the number of things, it's about whether there are any problems. Is there any? Basically, no.

So it's not dependent on how you choose your strategy. It's hard for you to keep it on the table, right? Is this a place that makes people desperate? It's not that desperate. People can die from old age. Companies can also die from old age. There is nothing more normal than this. That's why new companies have opportunities and young people have dreams.

一、曾鸣的独特之处：理论与实践的结合

Professor Zeng, I've heard many entrepreneurs mention you. They say that a very important strategic transformation may come from your classes at Hupan University. There are many business professors. I'm wondering why so many entrepreneurs have been influenced by you. What do you think is the difference between you and other business professors?

I think I'm very lucky. When the Internet was at its fastest development, I had the opportunity to join Ali. I was in a phase of the company's rapid development. So that experience, plus my good academic training, combined these two, made me integrate theory and practice. I often think about what I used to say and what I can use. I also think about what new things I can use in the future. The combination of theory and time is a big breakthrough.

The second point is that I have been studying the advanced industrial development. So when I talk to entrepreneurs, I can discuss their strategies and how to develop the next industry. What strategy do you use to make decisions that are more appropriate? So combining these two is also a very rare ability.

二、回望阿里：三次关键战略决策

For example, Ali is the company you have been involved in for the longest time. In the past 20 years, do you think it has affected Ali's strategy of survival?

I have been doing a review recently. I have been involved in Ali's previous 15 years more comprehensively. In fact, the most important decision is to create Taobao, create Alibabao, and create AliYun. And these three decisions were not only not recognized by the whole society at the time, but also very, very intense internal disputes within the company.

So everyone may have a lot of understanding of this dispute with Alibaba. But when Taobao announced its establishment, there were several executives who were very, very opposed. Why? I think Alibaba's business is not mature yet. And then you go to the core main business of eBay. The risk is too great. So the most important thing is these three decisions.

Then maybe a little bit more like Taobao. How to become a platform for shopping and trading. Become an ecosystem that supports e-commerce development. Then how to all in, unlimited. I think these two decisions are actually very important. But the importance may not be that big.

But what I just said is that there is still a little bit to be added later. In fact, after you do this strategy, there is still a layer of decision. The decision of the fourth stage strategy is also very important. For example, early days of Aria, you only serve one scene or the structure at the beginning is to serve more scenes. The scene you serve is to serve Taobao or to serve search. Then open source or closed source. These are all very, very big second-stage strategic issues.

Then there was the change in the database. Do you want to make your own database? Then the calculation changed, and the storage changed. So that's when the "Go to IOE" was called out. It changed IBM, Oracle, and EMC. EMC is storage. So just like today, after the calculation is finished, storage is a new bottleneck. So in the process of strategy to the ground, there are many important decisions. The lower it is, the closer the strategy and tactics are combined. So it's not enough to make a big strategic decision. It's a very big challenge to see the results from the decision to the landing.

三、反共识与卓越

The moment of strategy to make a decision, how do you know this is a good strategy? Because there were a lot of disputes at that time. Generally, because there are a lot of strategies, how do you judge it is a good strategy?

I don't know. Because I believe, so I see. All the good things that have become real-time companies are all finally proved to be established in the anti-communist. Of course, there are also a lot of crazy ideas in the process. In fact, there is no such thing. This point must be emphasized. It's not a crazy idea. What we see is the so-called survival bias. What you see is the bias of the successful. The most successful business must be anti-communist. But anti-communism must not be successful.

But at that time, based on our own ability, we could see and we were willing to believe that it was that kind of picture. So to a large extent, it was actually about how to create the future. It's not a simple plan.

Can only anti-communist strategies succeed? Can there be a consensus strategy that can succeed? I'm on a consensus track, but I'm doing better than everyone else. Can it succeed? That's excellent. That's excellent, not outstanding. Yes. Outstanding must come from anti-communism.

四、面对 AI 时代：从困惑到框架

Today, in the era of AI, we have entered a new phase of the cycle of the cycle. It's also a new civilization, as you said. Do you feel confused and anxious? When a person like you who wants to design a strategy sees the future, how do you feel at this time?

It is indeed very confusing because you know that there will be many new things, but you don't know which ones are the little waves that are in the middle of the storm, which ones represent the future big waves. What will change, what will not change, this is very confusing.

What are the little waves and what are the big waves? Do you have any initial thoughts and judgments?

This is why I wrote this book. Because I've been thinking about this for the past few years. I often have some observations and insights that I think are good, but they may soon be denied. But this year, the first half of the year, it's more obvious that there are some trend-based signals. Converge 就是開始出現了類似的信號 然後我看到了一個可能的框架 是可以去解釋當下發生的很多事情 甚至去推演未來下一步的發展的。

So I don't feel anxious anymore. I understand what stage we are in and I know what to do.

The reason we are talking is that you recently published a new book, "Science". You said that this book was not written as a plan, but it was naturally created. And you have been thinking about many issues in the past six months. Can you introduce this book and your creative process?

My own business is strategy. So actually, what I talk to entrepreneurs about the most is the uncertainty of the AI era. How to make strategies in such a fast-changing environment? So this is starting to think more clearly. But what really makes the whole framework appear is that I think I probably understand what stage of development AI has entered in industrialization, and then the different operating rules of each stage. I think this is clear, it will have a more clear guidance meaning for the next three or five years.

五、产业发展的三阶段框架

So today's AI industrialization has developed to what stage? How do you separate this complete stage?

I actually did a very systematic research, from mobile Internet to PC Internet, then to PC. Including when I did cloud computing, actually the first industrial revolution, the second industrial revolution, the third industrial revolution, actually the whole history has been studied once.

So, roughly speaking, the emergence of new technologies, I'm talking about huge, universal technologies, subversive innovation. In fact, they have gone through three stages. It's very interesting.

  • 第一阶段：this technology is gradually accepted by society, and then it becomes the foundation of society. This is the first step.
  • 第二阶段：the foundation of this technology has produced a lot of new applications, that is, the era of the era of the era of the era.
  • 第三阶段：when these large applications appear, we need to find some more underlying methods to operate this new world. This is the third stage. I call the third stage the stage of native applications.

For example, with mobile Internet, it is the stage of native applications for Tiktok and Zijie.

Right, in the early days, for example, the Internet, young people today may have heard of the black-and-white mobile phones, but the black-and-white mobile phone is the first one to be called a smartphone. And it has been a monopoly for a long time, and the market has also been deeply affected. 一直到2010年,它还是美国市场智能手机的百分之四十几的市场占有份额。iPhone只有百分之二十几。实际上是到iPhone4以后,iPhone才开始领先,开始跑起来的。

So, in the first and second stages, after the iPhone, there was the App Store. After the App Store, there were these new generation of native applications. In the early stages, I actually invested in mobile internet. There was also Moji天氣 and a bunch of other applications. At that time, the Japanese market was already over 100 million. But we soon realized that they didn't represent the future. The primary application that really solves the core needs is the native application.

Why do you have to go through a major application outbreak first and then go to the native application? Why is the native application not born in the second stage?

Because the outbreak of applications gives the technology the direction of development in the next stage. After technology becomes a basic luxury, it is not that it can't be stopped. It has to find its own new direction of development. But in the end, it is not clear which direction to develop.

其实就像我刚讲的那个字节，其实是先做了今日头条，甚至在那之前还做了内涵段子，一堆的小的产品。是因为在那个技术的早期，你不知道哪个东西能 work，所以你要试不同的东西。第一阶段那个时候只有文字成熟了，所以才会出现今日头条。但是今日头条探索出了推荐算法，这样的一种新的 both technology and business models. And then, due to the expansion of bandwidth and the development of computing, short videos appeared. The combination of short videos and the underlying technology of recommended algorithms, the two combined to create a live-action native application like Tiktok. A real national-level application.

So, when the original application is built from the basic infrastructure, there is a transition stage in the middle. Can you call the second stage a transition stage?

You said that, many of the founders in the middle were so sad. So why would I hesitate? The second stage itself is very exciting and very valuable. So why did I say that the original stage is the third stage? In fact, I just want to tell everyone that there are still maybe 8 years or 10 years, a very wonderful time belongs to the second stage. You can't cross to the third stage. You can't cross it. There is no accumulation of the second stage. You can't cross to the third stage. And based on the accumulation of the first stage, what should be done now is what should be done in the second stage. App explosion.

六、当下的历史坐标：Token 化与浏览器时刻

In the current industry cycle of AI, have we finished the first stage? Or in the first stage or in the second stage? At what time point?

I think the first stage of the tokenization in 2026 is a standard stage. The core reason is that at the beginning of this year, you may remember that the word "token" has formed a wide consensus. There have been very close discussions for two or three months. Huang Lingxun said at the GTC conference in Invida that Invida's future is "token factory". And Sam also immediately expressed that OpenAI's core is to sell tokens.

Why is this token important? It is because when a technology has a standard quantity mark, it can be used in a standardized way. So we will talk about one degree of electricity today, right? This is a ton of water, a jB of flow, right? These are so that we can use a very simple technology that used to be very advanced. Today, everyone knows how many tokens I have, how many jobs I can do, how much money I can make. This thing has become a basic social facility. So this is the end of the first stage.

The first stage — We are now in the second stage?

What is interesting this year is that it is also the beginning of the second stage. Because before and after the Spring Festival, another thing that was very exciting was the open crowd. Everyone was raising lobsters, and they didn't sleep well during the Spring Festival. Everyone was doing crazy things every day. What did the lobsters show everyone? They showed the infinite potential of an agent who can complete tasks independently.

So that's why everyone is so excited. So I think the second stage of AI is the intelligent stage. The intelligent stage is the new applications of the AI era. So the first stage is already mature. And then we are now standing at the beginning of the second stage.

我们回到了浏览器出现之前

If you compare it to, for example, the year of the Internet, the year of mobile Internet, can you make such a comparison today? Of course, this is a bit of a price to pay, but we still want to compare.

This is a question I've been thinking about for 2-3 years. Actually, I did a talk show 2 years ago, where we were hugging Yahoo. Yahoo is coming soon. And at the beginning of this year, I felt a bit confused. How did we return to the browser stage? It seems to be earlier than Yahoo.

Your judgment is more suspicious. Yes, it is more suspicious. Because when I saw these things coming out of Open Cloud, my first reaction was — We are still waiting for a browser to come out. It's not that after the browser comes out, we are waiting for another browser to come out.

Why is there such a movement? It's because the word that appears at the same time as agent is skill. We think about what the essence of agent is. It's actually sharing ability. We put our knowledge and ability together and share it so that others can use it. Then OpenCloud provides a framework and ideas. The original ability can be sealed and used.

I suddenly thought of what I was most happy about in 1992. It's building a website. Oh, right. That's building a website. Everyone wants to build a website. Then what is the purpose of building a website? Just to share information. So the innovation of AGI has allowed us to enter the age of information and ability. We have processed a lot of information and knowledge. So it is no longer necessary to share information today. Everyone is asking the answer directly to the chat GPT. Everyone is no longer looking for information.

But today's big model can achieve this achievement because of the 1992 wars. Let everyone put all the information on the Internet. Complete the digitalization process of information. So we do the comparison. The key is when we make a copy without a custom-made keychain, so that we can understand the underlying operation pattern of the keychain after we draw the keychain model, instead of entangled in the form of technical performance.

So when I think about it, everyone is building, one is building a site, one is building an agent, and then one is sharing information, one is sharing capabilities, I think this structure is right.

浏览器与 Yahoo 的功能

Why is the browser important in that era? It's a new stage. The browser has completed two core functions. Through HTML and a lot of other things, it established a very simple unified standard for building a war. So there is no threshold for building a war. People with information can build a war. Originally, building a war was a professional work of a professional engineer. So he greatly reduced the threshold for creating it. That is, we are talking about today, the threshold for developers has been greatly reduced.

On the other hand, it has reduced the threshold of browsing websites. Because you only need to click to complete the entire process of information browsing. So you immediately get a notification from the user, and then the attack is also reported. Then there are endless websites, and then everyone doesn't know what to watch.

At this time, Yahoo appeared. Yahoo! was the first to tell you that the most interesting website was among the 100 websites that appeared today. When there were 10,000 websites, it told you what was the most interesting of the top 10. Then it divided the entertainment, news, and stock for you. So Yahoo! is actually a process of structural information. Yes, it is a path. It is in the business of cutting, not in the business of increasing, right? At the same time, there must be a commercialization to reduce the pressure on everyone's awareness.

We are still in the process of commercialization today. There are all kinds of skill outbreaks. Yes, because we just ask anyone around us, and they will not tell you who is the agent that he uses every day.

Who do you think will be able to commercialize this matter? Have you seen any Yahoo's exit? Is it the form of Open Cloud?

No, I haven't seen Yahoo's exit at all. So I said that even the browser has not appeared yet. So if you let me say it with my head, I think the next biggest opportunity is a similar opportunity like a browser. It will unite the standard of agents. Then at the same time it can let users use a very simple method to call an agent. Then there will be a large number of agents. This may be the most exciting thing in the next two years.

No, on both sides. Organizational culture is definitely one of the conditions. Because a company with 100,000 people turns into an AI origin, and a company with 10 people turns into an AI origin company with 1,000 people. The difficulty is different. This is a very important point.

The second is that — This is the understanding of the platform and the ecosystem. If you don't make the first real successful agent, you probably don't understand how the agent is run. You can't provide the basic facilities and become the standard. You can't become the gateway. So you have to really understand the agent. Only when you have users can you attract more people. The developer of more agents is developing on you. So, having a successful agent is a prerequisite.

That's why there's a black hole effect. Yes.

XAI 与 Meta 掉队的原因

You see, in the past two years, XCI has also done a lot of things. Do you think they are wrong in their strategy?

There may be problems in their strategy. They don't have a particularly clear direction. It's not as focused as Slopec. And then I think there must be problems in the organization.

Let me give you a little detail. I only met a group of engineers in Gui Gu. The person of XAI is always the most tired person. Oh, he is the most tired. Yes, he is not the most tired person. He is just over-exploited. Maybe the way he works with Aaron is also over-exploited. Although he may let you grow, he may be very over-exploited. So when you see them coming, you don't have the strength to speak.

Any organization's innovation is actually like human beings. When people are too tired, there is no innovation. You must be in a relatively open and relaxed state, you will have new things come out. When an organization is so tight and then under a very high pressure environment, it is a very difficult thing to do a special innovation.

And I heard the researchers' evaluation and did not feel that Iran really understood the big model. So his original method theory is that he is more biased against hardware. In fact, in this era of AI, He can't give the answer directly to himself. And he can't use a co-created way to let the organization give the organizational way to give the answer. Because he used to be down to earth, right? Yes, he gave the answer with low principle. And then forced everyone to do it super regularly. But in this situation, he can't give the answer himself. He doesn't give the people down there so much space to give an answer.

I think XAS is definitely stuck in the organization. So this is also the relationship between the organization and the strategy. It's very bad. Yes, yes. He didn't create a strategy through the organization. It's all his own will. Yes.

What about Ma Yitang?

I always think that Xiaozha is very young. Why can't he keep up?

No, you are young, but you are early to consume. Oh, it's consuming a lot. Because you are being one generation after another. In fact, it is consuming the potential of your knowledge. And the Meta is so big that its internal transfer resources become very difficult. And I think most researchers don't think that Xiaozha understands models. So he can't make a really important decision.

Then the other two companies, for example, Sam, he really relies on Ilya, and Ilya can really drive the whole thing. And Sam is a good CEO, so these two are a good match. And Anthropic has a very strong overall governance ability. Then Daryl gave Mission Vision more accurate control. So Anthropic showed a very focused and vision-driven company's explosive power.

But because OpenAI has a thick base, even if it chases Anthropic in this round, it will be very fast. But these two companies are essentially new-generation startup companies, so their organizational culture is actually more compatible in all aspects. Then you go to other companies and you have your own problems.

中国公司的观察

What about Chinese companies? Do you have any observations?

Chinese companies are actually similar. Basically similar. Kimmy may be a little more primitive, but Qianwen started earlier and has the support of big companies. So he can keep moving forward. Then when Zhang Yiming reacted to it and wanted to all-in, the speed of the self-created was also very fast.

Why is the competition in China very slow every time it is connected? It's because the first-time companies are not like American companies. It has a two or three-year first-time period, so it has a healthy DNA stage. Then Chinese companies, at least so far, 还是在美国原型上的一个快速跟进。对。所以大家同时起步的话，就必然变成百团大战。嗯。因为大家看到的都是差不多的图像，然后都去硅谷把所有研究员都录一遍，然后每个人都能挖一两个人，所以就变成了相对容易出现统治化竞争的。

但是这里面，即使是这样，这里面真正认知比较深刻的, and then maybe a year or half earlier, right? Like Yang Zhiling and Yan Junjie, including these few, in fact, they are more distant. It's not so much about the competition that follows, but they are ahead.

Now we shouldn't do the big model anymore, right? Go to participate in this.

I don't think there will be anyone doing the big model in the traditional sense. There will be no one to vote. Unless you are a new lab.

Xiao Hong said you still have it. They are all doing it. No, their core is all about applications. They are all doing big models. No, they do big models to supplement some basic capabilities. It's to be able to exert force when doing real applications. This is different from other two companies. So you didn't see too many of their teams coming out to play parameters. Right? It is a backup of its future basic capabilities.

I don't think these two companies are willing to participate in the competition of big models as a basic infrastructure API factory. But at least they think that the premise of doing applications is that I have to have a very strong model. In the next stage, the boundary between the model and application technology of big applications is unclear. So if they are too strong in this generation, they may not be able to keep up with the next generation.

Yes, so this is what we discussed earlier. Do you want to make a model? So it's a budget of ability. But this is also an open discussion. It's about what stage the actual progress will be. It's like this chess is not in the middle of the game, it's still in the opening stage.

十七、未来社会：从生产革命到创造力革命

Do you have any predictions for this year's model, agent, or robot?

I never make short-term predictions. I only provide some regular understanding for everyone's reference. For example, what about five years? I think agent's entrance will definitely appear in five years. The second stage is probably I think everyone can understand.

Of course, mobile Internet is really like the product of Tiktok and Pinduoduo. It's going to be the third. Yes, Google, Tiktok, Tiktok and Pinduoduo are similar. And you think Pinduoduo came out very late. Yes, how many years is it now?

That may be eight years or ten years later. It's so long. But it has provided a lot of hope for app entrepreneurs. Don't forget that OpenAI has been 11 years. It's just the acceleration we've felt in the past two years.

When AI becomes a new production material and infrastructure, how long does society need to digest this technological revolution?

A generation. A generation. 20 years. Because they are the original residents.

德鲁克框架与创造力时代

If AI can be obtained from outside like energy, what is the difference between the future people and people?

I think it's the difference in creativity. So, there is a very classic analysis framework in Deluc. It has drawn three stages of human society since the industrial era. The first stage is the production revolution, which is the replacement of hand-made houses by water lines. The second stage is the management revolution, which started about 100 years ago. There are these scientific management methods of Thaler, and then the new kind of business school appeared. The core purpose of the business school is to match modern management with — This management staff. The third stage is called the stage of knowledge revolution. That is, he observed that from the 70s onward software becomes a very important direction of development. And the core of software is to deal with human knowledge. To immerse knowledge and the most practical through software methods. Become a standard implementation method.

This is DeLuca, he died in 1999. So I saw the changes of the past two centuries. So I take advantage of his framework. I think from the perspective of people, the era of AI can be defined as the era of creativity. All knowledge that can be structured will be controlled by AI. Then people are forced to develop their new potentials. But you can also say that people are finally released and can develop their potentials. I think this space is very large. This direction is creativity. It's something that AI can't do.

It's just that we need to have a better understanding and re-defining of creativity. Creativity may not be simply writing songs or painting. It may be more about original definition and the ability to solve complex problems. For example, after the real invention of electricity and the emergence of water supply, there will be the concept of industrial function. 技术功能的概念，然后才有了白领。这些都是 19 世纪的人其实根本想象不到的事情。

所以我觉得未来所有人努力的方向就是开发自己的创造力。

这个创造力还是一种原创造力。

对，当然了，当然了，就是无中生有的能力。有的东西机器都知道啊。一种无中生有的能力。对。Because if there is already something, the machine has already taken it as data. This kind of creation may be very boring from the perspective of the machine, because it may be all kinds of emotional companionship between people. There are all kinds of things that I want. There are all kinds of things that I didn't need to be developed before. That is to say, maybe not contributing to the great progress of this physical world, but it may be a great contribution to the growth and happiness of mankind. There are many ways to help. There are many ways that we have not thought of before.

商学院、办公楼与教育系统

You just said that if the company disappears, will the business school disappear?

Business schools are no longer working. They are all falling apart.

The office that is being built around the company, will these visible changes happen?

Yes, they will. Because the proportion of the virtual world will be higher and higher. The proportion of the virtual world will be higher and higher. Yes. The direction of Metaverse is correct. It may only take five years.

What changes can you see in the future as a society?

There will be changes all over the world. I met some entrepreneurs who want to do this land application. The world they imagined is not what we can understand now.

Interesting. I think today you are still very optimistic about the future.

I am optimistic. I always think there is a huge space for development.

Will it change the entire education system? If the demand for human ability is high, will the previous education system still be a kind of IQ? It is essentially the knowledge of the book. IQ development is the second place. Knowledge of the book is the first place.

This is definitely not possible. Look at how many interests we have been suppressed since we were young. We did not develop our potentials along the path of open exploration. We were all pressed into the fixed mode of the original world in order not to lose on the starting line at the earliest time.

So I think the biggest conflict is the conflict of the education system. Because young people already know that the future is completely different from what we imagine today. So you can ask any high school student, they probably know how to find a job after graduating from college. They may have a lot of ideas, but we definitely don't dare to let them go their way. So they are stuck here. But if you ask younger parents, how should I educate my newborn child? He must know how to educate in a new way. He just doesn't know how to educate.

So this is a special need for the next generation of society to spend a lot of resources and energy to explore the direction of the five elements. The ability to live and die.

Yes, this is a good summary. Yes, yes. Some AI have people need to do the five elements. Yes.

人机关系的未来

How will the relationship between people and systems and people and AI evolve in the future?

I think it's a very clear relationship within the organization. It's a deep relationship. At least we don't talk about the ASI, super-autonomous intelligence, what it looks like. Anyway, we don't agree. We don't talk about that first.

In this era of AGI, it will definitely penetrate into all aspects of society. Just like we can't live without mobile phones in the past ten years. In the future, everyone hang a camera on a certain place, have a voice-receiving device, and then wearable things are all over the body. People who are on the outer frame of the frame become people who are on the enhanced version. I think this is completely imaginable.

Have you seen any good hardware companies?

Hardware products are actually the hot spot of the past year or two. All kinds of consumer hardware are in the process of being produced. Just like we said, after 00 years, everyone is doing electricity, home appliances. But in the end, there are several major categories that can be established. There are countless small categories. I don't know what it will be now. Just like the one that appeared in the United States a long time ago, the one that baked bread machine. Everyone still uses it now. That was also invented a long time ago. But that is not big enough, the technology is not complicated enough. So he can't raise a big company.

拥抱不确定性

So there are a lot of new companies. In fact, everything I said will be 重新来一次。但是哪些是大东西，哪些是小东西，哪些是主，哪些是辅，然后谁用哪种方法，找到了面向未来的密码，这个都是不确定的。

但是我觉得有个基本态度要改变，就是原来我们倾向于降低不确定性，但是我觉得在这个阶段，其实是要拥抱不确定性。不确定性就是最大的机会。

所以心态先得改了，就不能恐惧。When you see uncertainty and complexity, you are afraid. You will definitely not be able to move forward. But when you face huge uncertainty and complexity, you feel particularly fun and have a chance to create something new. I think that is the mentality of these entrepreneurs in the younger generation. We are a little bit up in the air. We are too worried about them.

Mr. Ziming, what is your mission?

I think it's just being a happy researcher.

Happy researcher. Yes, I think in this context, it's a very interesting positioning.

A happy researcher. Will AI make humans happier?

At least that's what I hope. This is what everyone is talking about, AI is like a mountain. But it will definitely bring a series of new problems. But overall — We can discuss this on a more philosophical level, but on a philosophical level, the progress of civilization is that technology constantly brings new possibilities. And people can cultivate new technologies and enter a new stage of civilization development.

Is the happiness index of new civilization higher or lower than that of old civilization?

If it's not easy to say from a philosophical point of view, but from a general measurement index, it must be improved. If you think about it, if you say there is no air conditioning now, what will you feel? And then when you have a problem of temperature and temperature in the agricultural era for tens of thousands of years, the industrial era basically solved the problem of temperature and temperature in a scale. Then the consumer era solved the problem of insufficient consumption. But now it's basically too much supply and demand. Our core is at least in the physical product stage, basically too much supply and demand. Then the Internet solved the problem of asymmetric information — that everyone in the world can share. So we have made a big step forward. AI is definitely when we have so many smart solutions, we can do something more interesting.

One of the organization's evaluation standards in the future is whether people can be happier in one of them. It's been like this since Google started. That is, everyone may not have the feeling now. In fact, Google in 2007 and 2008 was as godlike as the two companies today. — So the culture at that time, Google was the first to mention it, and it felt like the future. So they were the first to mention it. That's called the Internet era. In fact, it requires a new culture and a new way of organizing. That trend will continue.

十八、快问快答

I'm curious about the typical day of Professor Zeng Ming. What is it like to be a happy researcher?

In fact, the first thing is to talk to entrepreneurs and see their latest ideas. The second is to look at the latest information, and look at interviews like yours, because it really helped me save a lot of things. Now I can see a very complete dialogue of thoughts. So it means that I have a lot of information input, and I can do data training, so that I am not so tired and not so hard. Otherwise, I think most people have a deep feeling in the first half of this year. That is, you are very easy to be affected by AI.

I have some quick questions and answers. What is your favorite food in the global market?

We are trying to leave more memories of the carbon-free civilization before the return of the Earth's life. Chili grass road.

A place you like in the global scope.

It's still Shanghai.

Do you usually read AI papers? What do you think is the most important AI paper?

I don't read AI technical papers.

What is a key and important "BET" in your current understanding?

There is a well-used "to see" agent.

Our company is called "Language and World." When you first heard this name, what did you think?

I might change to "Smartphone and World."

Can you share a few books? Your life books that really had a big impact on you?

I think management books are relatively basic. Like the series of "Long Life." And like the book of DeLuke. And then when I was in my major — Basically a book that was completely overwritten. Because there were too many disasters, I copied Friedman's book on market basic operating mechanism. It's not thick, but it's particularly exciting. So that's what I learned about the market's basic operating mechanism.

关于管理与战略的启蒙

What do you think made you so interested in management and strategy?

Actually, I gave up the science of science in high school. I took part in these outdoor competitions. Because we were probably the first science division. I actually liked history and humanities more. Although I was the first one to go on that path, I was not interested in it. I gave up in high school. After I chose economics in college, I found that I had more math requirements than most of the science subjects. I thought it was too boring. So when I was studying for my PhD, I chose business school. And I chose a major that was relatively popular in the strategic field. And then I had to establish a connection between the real world and the theoretical world. I think this is more fun.

So there are not many people in the founding people who have strategic ability. Those who have gone far, such as those who have achieved their goals, goals, and strategies, those who have achieved their goals are already very good. But not the top ones. The top ones are strictly speaking, those who have achieved their goals are the ones who are likely to go to the top.

Some people may have goals first and then slowly develop their goals. Some people are born to achieve their goals. Or, if you form a very rare team, there are one or two people who form a very good complement. One person may be a little stronger in fighting, and the other person is a little stronger in fighting. It's a combination that's a little bit like Wang Xin and Wang Huiwen. It's also a very rare combination.

关于张一鸣

What is the drive of the self-destruction?

It's hard to say, because I don't have much personal communication with Zhang Yiming. So I can't judge his fate. But Zhang Yiming is an amazing genius. He has his own management philosophy. At least he is willing to take action. He has a complete understanding of the organization. Including the company-level products he proposed at the beginning. This is already very leading. Including, for example, what I used to say about Netflix, the culture of Netflix. Most people's first reaction is that the Chinese people can't do it. Because that culture is too American and ancient. But ZJ is the earliest. Basically, it is very similar to the culture of the Internet flying.

But ZJ finally made a efficiency factory. Because he only understood everything. The rest is to pursue efficiency in the strategic implementation stage. So his AI strategy needs to be re-designed by Zhang Yiming.

Any company will pursue efficiency in the end. Because your strategy is getting clearer and clearer. The rest is the implementation.

But as we just said, the fate of the organization is that the times will change. Make you the original one is not suitable. So you either turn your back on the world or get eliminated by the times.

Yes, everyone is very fair in this era. This sounds like good news.
